ai.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
ai.brief: Accurate, up-to-date climate projections are essential for planning decisions that enhance the resilience of power grids, protect public health, maximize agricultural yields, and more. Now, MIT researchers have developed a technique that streamlines the production of fast, trustworthy, and adaptable artificial intelligence models for climate prediction. These specialized AI models, known as climate emulators, can rapidly simulate the effects of human activities onto a future climate, predicting impacts on temperatures or sea level, for example. Because emulators run in a matter of seconds, scientists use them to efficiently test thousands of varied climate scenarios. This provides more reliable estimates and can identify unexpected outcomes of regional interventions. The MIT researchers developed a training technique that boosts the performance and adaptability of a climate emulator while using only a fraction of the data typically required. This significantly cuts production time for these practical scientific tools.
